intro: Hi! In this lesson you learn the words you need for life online: posting, sharing and following on social media, describing what's wrong when your phone or laptop has a problem, and talking about the news. Warm-up: what's the first app you open in the morning, and where do you get your news?
teachingNotes: Teach the words in small themed groups with an Indonesian gloss: social media (post, share, like, comment on, follow, followers, DM, notification, privacy settings, scroll), going viral (go viral, trending, influencer, content creator, go live, stream), devices and problems (phone, charger, charge, battery runs out, signal, Wi-Fi password, storage is full, crash, freeze, isn't working, error message) and fixes (restart, update, back up), and the news (headline, article, breaking news, report, journalist, current events, according to, fake news, hoax). The learner already met email, app, password, file, download/upload, attach a file and log in vs login in a2-vocab-work-study: recap in a line, don't reteach.

Social media: post, like, share and comment are both nouns and verbs (a post / to post). You comment ON something (*'He commented my photo' → He commented on my photo). Common error: *'The video is very viral'. In Indonesian 'viral' works like an adjective with sangat; in English a video GOES viral (went viral, has gone viral, will go viral). Viral before a noun is fine: a viral video. Trap: Indonesian 'live di IG' → I'll go live on Instagram (not *I'll live on Instagram: live = tinggal). 'It's trending' is fine.

Devices and problems. Common error: *'My laptop is error'. Error is a noun (a thing), not a describing word: say My laptop isn't working / My laptop shows an error (message) / I get an error message. HP is Indonesian (and an American computer brand): say phone, mobile (British) or cell phone (American); 'handphone' is used in Singapore and Malaysia but most English speakers don't say it. Battery: runs out / is low / is dead (US) / is flat (UK), informal 'my phone died'. charger (alat cas) is the thing, charge (ngecas) the action. Phones use 'storage is full' (memori penuh). crash (an app suddenly closes) and freeze, past froze (the screen stops; Indonesian 'nge-hang') overlap in many sentences: accept either and never test them against each other. back up (verb, two words) / a backup (noun, one word) follows the same pattern as log in / login. Common error recap: *'I can't login' → I can't log in.

News: news ends in -s but is uncountable and singular: The news IS good, good news, some news, a piece of news, never *a news or *the news are. Fake news works the same (That's fake news, not *a fake news). Indonesian 'hoaks' = a hoax (countable), but fake news or misinformation is more common in English. according to + a source (according to Kompas, according to BMKG); for your own opinion say In my opinion / I think, not *according to me. Also: headline, article, breaking news, report (noun and verb), journalist (wartawan), current events, follow the news.

Limits: A0–A2 grammar only (present and past simple and continuous, present perfect with just/already/yet, going to, will, can/could, should, have to, zero and first conditional). No passive (avoid 'my account was hacked', 'it was shared 1,000 times'), no past perfect, no reported speech with tense changes (use According to … or The news says …), no second conditional, no relative clauses. Don't test near-synonyms against each other: crash/freeze, restart/turn it off and on again, post/upload/share, article/report, journalist/reporter.

keyPoints.title: The internet and social media
keyPoints.explanation: post, like, share and comment are nouns and verbs: post a photo, get 100 likes, share a link, comment on a post. follow someone → you are one of their followers. Send someone a DM (direct message). Turn off notifications, check your privacy settings, scroll through Instagram. A video goes viral (went viral), not 'is very viral'; a viral video is fine. Influencers and content creators go live (siaran langsung) or stream.

examples.en: Rina posted a photo of her new café, and it got 300 likes.
examples.id: Rina mengunggah foto kafe barunya, dan dapat 300 like.

examples.en: Send me a DM if you want the price.
examples.id: Kirim DM ke saya kalau mau tahu harganya.

examples.en: Her dance video went viral in two days.
examples.id: Video dansanya viral dalam dua hari.

id.title: Internet dan media sosial
id.explanation: post, like, share dan comment bisa jadi kata benda dan kata kerja: post a photo (unggah foto), get 100 likes (dapat 100 like), share a link (bagikan tautan), comment on a post (komen di postingan). follow someone (ikuti seseorang) → kamu salah satu followers-nya (pengikut). Kirim DM (direct message, pesan langsung). Matikan notifications (notifikasi), cek privacy settings (pengaturan privasi), scroll (menggulir) Instagram. Sebuah video goes viral (went viral = jadi viral), bukan 'is very viral'; a viral video (video viral) boleh. Influencer dan content creator go live (siaran langsung) atau stream.

keyPoints.title: Devices and technical problems
keyPoints.explanation: Your phone (not 'HP') needs a charger; the battery runs out; there's no signal; you ask for the Wi-Fi password; the storage is full. Problems: an app crashes, the screen freezes (froze), the laptop isn't working or shows an error message, not 'is error'. Fixes: restart it, update the app, back up your files, log in again (two words).

examples.en: My laptop isn't working. It shows an error every time I open Excel.
examples.id: Laptop saya error. Selalu muncul pesan error setiap kali saya buka Excel.

examples.en: The app crashed, so I restarted my phone.
examples.id: Aplikasinya tiba-tiba tertutup, jadi saya nyalakan ulang HP saya.

examples.en: Back up your photos before you update your phone.
examples.id: Cadangkan foto-fotomu sebelum kamu memperbarui HP-mu.

id.title: Perangkat dan masalah teknis
id.explanation: Phone-mu (bukan 'HP') butuh charger (alat cas); baterainya runs out (habis); tidak ada signal (sinyal); kamu minta Wi-Fi password; storage (memori penyimpanan) penuh. Masalah: aplikasi crashes (tiba-tiba tertutup), layar freezes (macet, nge-hang; lampau: froze), laptop isn't working (tidak berfungsi) atau shows an error message (menampilkan pesan error), bukan 'is error'. Solusi: restart (nyalakan ulang), update (perbarui) aplikasinya, back up (cadangkan) file-mu, log in lagi (dua kata).

keyPoints.title: News and current events
keyPoints.explanation: headline (the title in big letters), article, breaking news (news that is happening now), report (a noun and a verb), journalist, current events, follow the news. News looks plural but it's singular and uncountable: the news is, good news, never 'a news'. Fake news works the same; a hoax (hoaks) is countable. Give a source with according to: according to Kompas. For your own opinion, say In my opinion, not 'according to me'.

examples.en: I read the headlines on my phone every morning.
examples.id: Saya membaca judul-judul berita di HP setiap pagi.

examples.en: The news is on at seven.
According to the weather app, it's going to rain this afternoon.
examples.id: Menurut aplikasi cuaca, sore ini akan hujan.

id.title: Berita dan peristiwa terkini
id.explanation: headline (judul berita, huruf besar di atas), article (artikel), breaking news (berita yang sedang terjadi sekarang), report (laporan; melaporkan), journalist (wartawan), current events (peristiwa terkini), follow the news (mengikuti berita). News kelihatan jamak, tapi sebenarnya tunggal dan tidak bisa dihitung: the news is, good news, tidak pernah 'a news'. Fake news (berita palsu) juga begitu; a hoax (hoaks) bisa dihitung. Sebut sumbernya dengan according to (menurut): according to Kompas. Untuk pendapatmu sendiri, bilang In my opinion (menurut saya), bukan 'according to me'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one word: I never ___ photos of my children on Instagram. I want to protect their privacy.
guidedPractice.hint: What do you do when you put a photo on social media for other people to see? The verb is the same as the noun 'a post'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete: Only my friends can see my posts. I changed my privacy ___ last week.
guidedPractice.hint: The page in the app where you choose who can see your posts: privacy s… (pengaturan privasi). There are many options, so it's plural.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one word: There's no ___ in the basement car park, so I can't make a call.
guidedPractice.hint: Indonesian has almost the same word: sinyal.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one word: A ___ is a person who writes news articles or reports the news on TV.
guidedPractice.hint: In Indonesian: wartawan. The English word starts with j.

independentPractice.prompt: Write in English, for the end of a shop's poster: Ikuti kami di Instagram!
independentPractice.hint: follow = mengikuti. On social media we use on: on Instagram, on TikTok.

independentPractice.prompt: Write in English: Laptop saya nge-hang, jadi saya restart.
expected: my laptop froze so i restarted it
my laptop crashed so i restarted it
my laptop hung so i restarted it
my laptop froze so i restarted
my laptop crashed so i restarted
my laptop froze so i turned it off and on again
independentPractice.hint: nge-hang = freeze (past: froze). It happened already, so use the past simple: froze, restarted.

independentPractice.prompt: Complete the TV screen text: Breaking ___: big earthquake in Sulawesi.
independentPractice.hint: Breaking ___ = news that is happening right now (berita terkini).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: My cousin's video about street food in Medan was very viral last month.
acceptableAnswers: my cousin's video about street food in medan went viral last month
my cousins video about street food in medan went viral last month
last month my cousin's video about street food in medan went viral
assessment.rubric: Correct: … went viral last month (a video goes viral; last month = past simple went). 'became viral' = 60. 'was viral' = 50 (still not the natural chunk). 'goes viral' or 'has gone viral' with 'last month' = 60 (right chunk, wrong tense). Unchanged ('was very viral') = 0.

assessment.prompt: 50,000 people follow Pak Hasan's cooking account on Instagram, so they see all his new posts. Complete: His account has 50,000 ___.
acceptableAnswers: followers
assessment.rubric: Correct: followers (people who follow an account = pengikut). 'follower' = 60 (needs -s: 50,000). 'follows' = 30. 'fans' or 'subscribers' = 40 (subscribers is the YouTube word). 'likes' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: My laptop is error, so I can't finish the report.
acceptableAnswers: my laptop isn't working so i can't finish the report
my laptop is not working so i can't finish the report
my laptop isn't working so i cannot finish the report
my laptop is not working so i cannot finish the report
my laptop isnt working so i cant finish the report
my laptop doesn't work so i can't finish the report
my laptop does not work so i cannot finish the report
my laptop shows an error so i can't finish the report
my laptop is showing an error so i can't finish the report
my laptop shows an error message so i can't finish the report
my laptop has an error so i can't finish the report
there's an error on my laptop so i can't finish the report
assessment.rubric: Correct: My laptop isn't working / shows an error, so I can't finish the report (error is a thing, a noun, so it can't follow is like a describing word). 'My laptop is broken' = 80 (good English, but broken means physically damaged). 'My laptop has error' (no an) = 70. 'My laptop errors' = 30. Unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: There's no space left for new photos. The storage on my phone is ___.
acceptableAnswers: full
assessment.rubric: Correct: full (storage is full = memori penuh). 'low' = 60 (people say low on storage, but no space left = full). 'fully' = 50. 'finished', 'over' or 'empty' = 0. 'error' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: Before you sell your old phone, ___ up your photos and contacts. If you don't, you'll lose them.
acceptableAnswers: back
assessment.rubric: Correct: back (back up = mencadangkan, two words as a verb). 'backup' = 60 (one word is the noun: a backup). 'save' = 30 ('save up' means menabung uang). 'clean' or 'pick' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: ___ to BMKG, it will rain heavily in Jakarta tomorrow afternoon.
acceptableAnswers: according
assessment.rubric: Correct: According (according to + a source = menurut). 'Accordingly' = 40. 'Based' = 30 (based on, not based to). 'Following' or 'Thanks' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: I have a good news for you: you got the job!
acceptableAnswers: i have good news for you you got the job
i have some good news for you you got the job
i have a piece of good news for you you got the job
i've got good news for you you got the job
i've got some good news for you you got the job
i have got good news for you you got the job
assessment.rubric: Correct: I have (some) good news for you (news is uncountable: no a/an). 'I have a good new' = 0. 'I have good newses' = 20. 'I have the good news' = 50. Unchanged = 0.

material.title: Social media: post, share, comment, follow

id.title: Media sosial: post, share, comment, follow

blocks.text:
You already know *email, app, password, download, upload* and **log in** (two words when it's an action). Now the words for social media. Many are the same in Indonesian, so the job is to use them in the right **chunk** (words that go together).

Some words are a **noun** (a thing) and a **verb** (an action) at the same time:
- **a post** / **to post** (unggah): *I posted a photo.*
- **a like** / **to like**: *The photo got 200 likes.*
- **share** (bagikan): *Can you share the link?*
- **a comment** / **to comment on** (komen): *She commented on my post.* Don't forget **on**.

More words:
- **follow** (ikuti) → **followers** (pengikut): *I follow her on TikTok. She has 10,000 followers.*
- **a DM** = a direct message (pesan langsung): *Send me a DM.*
- **notifications** (notifikasi): *I turned off my notifications.*
- **privacy settings** (pengaturan privasi): *Check your privacy settings.*
- **scroll** (menggulir): *I scroll through Instagram before bed.*

id.text:
Kamu sudah tahu *email, app, password, download, upload* dan **log in** (dua kata kalau artinya tindakan). Sekarang kata-kata untuk media sosial. Banyak yang sama dengan bahasa Indonesia, jadi tugasnya adalah memakainya dalam **paket** yang benar (kata-kata yang biasa dipakai bersama).

Ada kata yang bisa jadi **kata benda** (benda) sekaligus **kata kerja** (tindakan):
- **a post** / **to post** (unggah): *I posted a photo.*
- **a like** / **to like**: *The photo got 200 likes.*
- **share** (bagikan): *Can you share the link?*
- **a comment** / **to comment on** (komen): *She commented on my post.* Jangan lupa **on**.

Kata lainnya:
- **follow** (ikuti) → **followers** (pengikut): *I follow her on TikTok. She has 10,000 followers.*
- **a DM** = direct message (pesan langsung): *Send me a DM.*
- **notifications** (notifikasi): *I turned off my notifications.*
- **privacy settings** (pengaturan privasi): *Check your privacy settings.*
- **scroll** (menggulir): *I scroll through Instagram before bed.*

rows.en: Rina posted a photo of her new café.
rows.id: Rina mengunggah foto kafe barunya.

rows.en: My boss commented on my LinkedIn post.
rows.id: Bos saya komen di postingan LinkedIn saya.

rows.en: Follow us on Instagram for new promos.
rows.id: Ikuti kami di Instagram untuk promo terbaru.
rows.note: on Instagram, on TikTok, on YouTube

id.note: on Instagram, on TikTok, on YouTube (pakai on)

rows.en: I don't post my address online. I check my privacy settings every month.
rows.id: Saya tidak mengunggah alamat saya di internet. Saya cek pengaturan privasi setiap bulan.

rows.en: Sorry, I didn't see your DM. My notifications were off.
rows.id: Maaf, saya tidak lihat DM-mu. Notifikasi saya mati.

blocks.explain: The verb is comment ON something: commented on my photo. Indonesian 'komen fotoku' has no word for on, so learners leave it out. 'comment' without -ed is also wrong here: it already happened.

id.explain: Kata kerjanya comment ON sesuatu: commented on my photo. Bahasa Indonesia 'komen fotoku' tidak punya kata untuk on, jadi orang sering melupakannya. 'comment' tanpa -ed juga salah di sini: kejadiannya sudah lewat.

blocks.text:
In Indonesian we say *videonya **sangat** viral*. In English, viral is something that **happens**: a video **goes viral** (menjadi viral, menyebar cepat).
- *It went viral.* (past: go → **went**)
- *It has gone viral.* (it's viral now)
- *If this video goes viral, …*

So not 'The video is very viral'. But wait: you **can** say **a viral video**. Before a noun (a thing), viral is fine: *a viral video, a viral post*. It's only 'is very viral' that sounds wrong.

People online:
- an **influencer**: a person with many followers who companies pay to talk about products
- a **content creator**: a person who makes videos or posts as a job

And **go live** (siaran langsung): *I'm going to go live on TikTok at 8.* Careful: 'I'll live on TikTok' means *saya akan tinggal di TikTok*, because **live** alone means tinggal. **stream** (streaming) works too: *They stream every night.* If many people are talking about something right now, it's **trending**.

id.text:
Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita bilang *videonya **sangat** viral*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, viral adalah sesuatu yang **terjadi**: sebuah video **goes viral** (menjadi viral, menyebar cepat).
- *It went viral.* (lampau: go → **went**)
- *It has gone viral.* (sekarang sudah viral)
- *If this video goes viral, …*

Jadi bukan 'The video is very viral'. Tapi tunggu: kamu **boleh** bilang **a viral video**. Sebelum kata benda (nama benda), viral boleh: *a viral video, a viral post*. Yang terdengar salah hanya 'is very viral'.

Orang-orang di internet:
- **influencer**: orang dengan banyak pengikut yang dibayar perusahaan untuk membicarakan produk
- **content creator**: orang yang membuat video atau postingan sebagai pekerjaan

Dan **go live** (siaran langsung, 'live'): *I'm going to go live on TikTok at 8.* Hati-hati: 'I'll live on TikTok' artinya *saya akan tinggal di TikTok*, karena **live** saja artinya tinggal. **stream** (streaming) juga bisa: *They stream every night.* Kalau banyak orang sedang membicarakan sesuatu sekarang, itu **trending**.

rows.en: Her video about cheap food in Bandung went viral.
rows.id: Videonya tentang makanan murah di Bandung jadi viral.

rows.en: Have you seen that viral video of the cat on the KRL?
rows.id: Kamu sudah lihat video viral kucing di KRL itu?
rows.note: viral before a noun is fine

rows.en: Sari is a content creator. She makes videos about make-up.
rows.id: Sari seorang content creator. Dia membuat video tentang make-up.

rows.en: The band is going to go live on YouTube tonight.
rows.id: Band itu akan siaran langsung di YouTube malam ini.

blocks.prompt: Dimas wants his followers to watch him play a game in real time. Complete: I'm going to ___ on TikTok at 9 p.m. Join me!
blocks.explain: Siaran langsung is go live. 'live' alone means tinggal (I live in Depok), and you can't plan to 'be very viral': a video goes viral if people share it.

id.prompt: Dimas ingin pengikutnya menonton dia main game secara langsung. Lengkapi: I'm going to ___ on TikTok at 9 p.m. Join me!
id.explain: Siaran langsung itu go live. 'live' saja artinya tinggal (I live in Depok), dan kamu tidak bisa merencanakan 'be very viral': video goes viral kalau orang-orang membagikannya.

blocks.text:
First, a trap: **HP** is Indonesian. In English, HP is a computer brand! Say **phone**, **mobile** (British) or **cell phone** (American). *Handphone* is used in Singapore and Malaysia, but most English speakers don't say it.

The words for your phone's everyday problems:
- **charger** (alat cas) is the thing; **charge** (ngecas) is the action: *I need to charge my phone. Have you got a charger?*
- the battery is **low** (lemah), then it **runs out** (habis): *My battery ran out.* People also say *my battery is dead* (American), *my battery is flat* (British) or simply *my phone died*.
- **signal** (sinyal): *There's no signal here.*
- the **Wi-Fi password**: *What's the Wi-Fi password?*
- **storage** (memori penyimpanan): *My storage is full.* (memori penuh)

id.text:
Pertama, satu jebakan: **HP** itu bahasa Indonesia. Dalam bahasa Inggris, HP adalah merek komputer! Bilang **phone**, **mobile** (British) atau **cell phone** (Amerika). *Handphone* dipakai di Singapura dan Malaysia, tapi kebanyakan penutur bahasa Inggris tidak memakainya.

Kata-kata untuk masalah HP sehari-hari:
- **charger** (alat cas) adalah bendanya; **charge** (ngecas) adalah tindakannya: *I need to charge my phone. Have you got a charger?*
- baterainya **low** (lemah), lalu **runs out** (habis): *My battery ran out.* Orang juga bilang *my battery is dead* (Amerika), *my battery is flat* (British) atau singkatnya *my phone died* (HP-ku mati).
- **signal** (sinyal): *There's no signal here.*
- **Wi-Fi password** (kata sandi Wi-Fi): *What's the Wi-Fi password?*
- **storage** (memori penyimpanan): *My storage is full.* (memori penuh)

rows.en: Can I charge my phone here? My battery is low.
rows.id: Boleh saya ngecas HP di sini? Baterai saya lemah.

rows.en: My phone died on the ojek, so I couldn't call you.
rows.id: HP saya mati di ojek, jadi saya tidak bisa menelepon kamu.

rows.en: There's no signal in the lift.
rows.id: Tidak ada sinyal di lift.

rows.en: I can't download the file. My storage is full.
rows.id: Saya tidak bisa mengunduh filenya. Memori saya penuh.

blocks.prompt: Your phone is at 2% and you're at a friend's house. Complete: Can I borrow your ___, please?
blocks.explain: The thing you plug in to charge a phone is a charger (alat cas). You can't borrow someone's signal or storage.

id.prompt: HP-mu tinggal 2% dan kamu di rumah teman. Lengkapi: Can I borrow your ___, please?
id.explain: Benda yang dicolok untuk mengecas HP adalah charger (alat cas). Sinyal atau memori orang lain tidak bisa dipinjam.

material.title: Problems and fixes: not 'my laptop is error'

id.title: Masalah dan solusinya: bukan 'my laptop is error'

blocks.text:
In Indonesian, **error** works like a describing word: *laptopnya error*. In English, **error** is a **noun** (a thing, like a message on the screen). So 'My laptop is error' is wrong. Say:
- **My laptop isn't working.** (tidak berfungsi)
- **My laptop shows an error.** / **I get an error message.** (muncul pesan error)

Other problems:
- an app **crashes** (tiba-tiba tertutup): *The app crashed.*
- the screen **freezes** (macet, nge-hang): *My laptop froze.* (freeze → **froze**, an irregular past)

And the fixes:
- **restart** (nyalakan ulang), or *turn it off and on again*
- **update** (perbarui): *update the app*; also a noun: *a new update*
- **back up** (cadangkan): *back up your photos*. Same pattern as **log in / login**: the action is two words (*back up*), the thing is one word (*a backup*).
- **log in** again: *I can't log in* (not 'I can't login').

id.text:
Dalam bahasa Indonesia, **error** dipakai seperti kata sifat: *laptopnya error*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **error** adalah **kata benda** (sebuah benda, misalnya pesan di layar). Jadi 'My laptop is error' salah. Bilang:
- **My laptop isn't working.** (tidak berfungsi)
- **My laptop shows an error.** / **I get an error message.** (muncul pesan error)

Masalah lain:
- aplikasi **crashes** (tiba-tiba tertutup): *The app crashed.*
- layar **freezes** (macet, nge-hang): *My laptop froze.* (freeze → **froze**, bentuk lampau tidak beraturan)

Dan solusinya:
- **restart** (nyalakan ulang), atau *turn it off and on again* (matikan lalu nyalakan lagi)
- **update** (perbarui): *update the app*; juga kata benda: *a new update* (pembaruan baru)
- **back up** (cadangkan): *back up your photos*. Polanya sama dengan **log in / login**: tindakannya dua kata (*back up*), bendanya satu kata (*a backup*).
- **log in** lagi: *I can't log in* (bukan 'I can't login').

rows.en: My printer isn't working. Can you help me?
rows.id: Printer saya error. Bisa bantu saya?

rows.en: I get an error message when I open the banking app.
rows.id: Muncul pesan error waktu saya buka aplikasi bank.
rows.note: an error: error is a thing, so it takes an

id.note: an error: error adalah benda, jadi pakai an

rows.en: The game froze, so I restarted my laptop.
rows.id: Gamenya nge-hang, jadi saya nyalakan ulang laptop saya.

rows.en: You should update the app. The old version crashes a lot.
rows.id: Sebaiknya kamu perbarui aplikasinya. Versi lamanya sering tiba-tiba tertutup.

rows.en: I back up my work files every Friday.
rows.id: Saya mencadangkan file kerja saya setiap Jumat.

blocks.prompt: WhatsApp says: 'A new version is available.' Complete: You should ___ the app.
blocks.explain: A new version means you update the app (perbarui). crash is a problem, not something you do on purpose, and error is a noun, not an action.

id.prompt: WhatsApp menampilkan: 'A new version is available.' Lengkapi: You should ___ the app.
id.explain: Versi baru artinya kamu update (perbarui) aplikasinya. crash adalah masalah, bukan sesuatu yang kamu lakukan dengan sengaja, dan error adalah kata benda, bukan tindakan.

material.title: The news: headlines, reports and 'according to'

blocks.text:
News words:
- **headline** (judul berita): the title in big letters at the top
- **article** (artikel): the text of a news story
- **breaking news** (berita terkini): news about something that is happening right now
- **report** (laporan, melaporkan): *a report on TV; Kompas reported the accident.*
- **journalist** (wartawan)
- **current events** (peristiwa terkini), **follow the news** (mengikuti berita)

A surprise: **news** ends in -s, but it's **not plural**. It's **uncountable** (a word we don't count one by one, like *water* and *homework*). So:
- **The news is** on at seven. (not 'the news are')
- I have **good news**. / **some news** / **a piece of news** (not 'a news')

**Fake news** (berita palsu) works the same: *That's fake news.* Indonesian *hoaks* is **a hoax** in English (countable: *It's a hoax*), but **fake news** or **misinformation** is more common.

To say where information comes from, use **according to** (menurut) + the source: *According to Detik, the toll road is closed.* For your own opinion, say **In my opinion** or **I think**, not 'according to me'.

id.text:
Kosakata berita:
- **headline** (judul berita): judul berhuruf besar di bagian atas
- **article** (artikel): teks sebuah berita
- **breaking news** (berita terkini): berita tentang sesuatu yang sedang terjadi sekarang
- **report** (laporan, melaporkan): *a report on TV; Kompas reported the accident.*
- **journalist** (wartawan)
- **current events** (peristiwa terkini), **follow the news** (mengikuti berita)

Satu kejutan: **news** berakhiran -s, tapi **bukan jamak**. Kata ini **uncountable** (tidak bisa dihitung satu per satu, seperti *water* dan *homework*). Jadi:
- **The news is** on at seven. (bukan 'the news are')
- I have **good news**. / **some news** / **a piece of news** (sebuah berita; bukan 'a news')

**Fake news** (berita palsu) juga begitu: *That's fake news.* *Hoaks* dalam bahasa Inggris adalah **a hoax** (bisa dihitung: *It's a hoax*), tapi **fake news** atau **misinformation** lebih sering dipakai.

Untuk menyebut asal informasi, pakai **according to** (menurut) + sumbernya: *According to Detik, the toll road is closed.* Untuk pendapatmu sendiri, bilang **In my opinion** atau **I think**, bukan 'according to me'.
